decisive_items: A 55-year-old man underwent right hemicolectomy for moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon
Thirteen months after surgery, follow-up CT revealed a 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
CTAP showed absence of the right portal vein and a perfusion defect throughout the right lobe, suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus
response.rationale: History of colorectal cancer and new liver lesion strongly suggest metastasis; portal vein thrombus is a complication, not the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Portal vein tumor thrombus is a complication, not the primary diagnosis.
HCC with PVTT is less likely given the history of colorectal cancer.
Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is less likely given the history of colorectal cancer.
HCC is less likely given the history of colorectal cancer.
